prompt: Explain why the authors say pure RL is hard to scale to tasks like writing, and how DeepSeek-R1 handles such tasks instead.

private.model_answer: Pure RL depends on a reliable reward signal. For math and code, rules or test cases give one, but for writing no dependable rule-based reward exists, and a model-based reward can be exploited by the policy, which finds shortcuts that score high without being truly better. So R1 uses human-annotated supervised data for such tasks and runs only a few hundred RL steps.

rubric.criterion: Says pure RL requires a reliable reward or verifier, which is hard to build for writing
Mentions that model-based rewards can be exploited (reward hacking)
States that R1 relies on human-annotated SFT data and only brief RL for such tasks
